title: P01 parameter-matched looped transformer: three unique Peri-LN blocks of width 384 (8 heads of 48) cycled A-B-C-A-B-C, six logical applications, 5,410,944 params vs 129-claude's six untied 256-wide blocks (4,800,000)
description: P01 (idea ID P01, the untried 'parameter-matched looping, wider shared blocks' piece): 125-fable showed full weight sharing at fixed depth (A-B-C-A-B-C at width 256, 2.43M params) reproduced the incumbent's pretraining and RL start with half the parameters (-14, noise-level), so this spends the freed budget on width: the same three-block cycle at d_model 384 (d_ff 1536, 8 heads of 48, same 4 ALiBi + 4 NoPE split, Muon/AdamW, LR floor 0.3 unchanged). Each of the six logical applications now has 2.25x the weights and FLOPs of an incumbent block at about the incumbent's unique parameter count (+13%), testing whether per-block capacity applied repeatedly beats per-depth specialization as the starting point for expert iteration on >=7-line proofs.
hypothesis: 125-fable established that sharing three blocks across six depths costs ~nothing on this task: the six depths do not need six different operators, so the per-depth parameters of the untied incumbent are partly redundant. If what limits transfer to >=7-line proofs is the capacity of the operator applied at each depth (wider residual stream carrying more simultaneous proof-state features, wider heads, wider MLP) rather than depth-specific specialization, then re-spending the halved budget on a 1.5x wider shared block should give a better fit per unique parameter and a stronger repeated refinement step, and the RL fine-tune should keep climbing on the harvested long proofs because the same block improves at every depth at once (a gradient from six applications per shared matrix). Failure modes: (a) wall-clock: 2.25x per-application FLOPs at a latency-bound size cut steps (110-claude at width 320 lost 16% of steps; expect 25-35% here), leaving an under-trained handoff with a weak round-1 harvest (parse failures >35%), the 110/127 pathology; (b) sharing is neutral and width alone is not the lever (103/124: MLP width moved the metric <=30), so this lands at 125's -14 plus noise; (c) slower sampling with 384-wide KV caches pushes a slow pod past the 2400 s cap (110 seed 1 timed out at 2495 s).
expected_delta: -45 to +40 theorems at >=7 vs 646 (central guess 0); pretrain steps ~2,800-3,300 (vs 129's 4,137-4,238), final val loss 0.078-0.092, held-out greedy 0.95-0.975, round-1 targets 520-700; total secs 1,750-2,200 (2.25x per-token FLOPs at decode, latency-bound), timeout risk on a slow pod

arch.type: gpt (fork model.py) ALiBiGPT with looped Peri-LN blocks
arch.pos: hybrid: ALiBi slopes 1/4..1/256 on 4 heads, NoPE (slope 0) on 4 heads, no RoPE (unchanged from 115-fable)
arch.norm: Peri-LN layernorm (pre-LN plus LayerNorm on both branch outputs), unchanged
arch.change: vs 129-claude: D 256 -> 384 (head dim 32 -> 48, d_ff 1024 -> 1536) and 6 untied blocks -> 3 unique blocks cycled A-B-C-A-B-C (N_UNIQUE = 3); everything else identical
arch.n_params_detail: 3 PeriLN blocks x 1,776,000 (12*384^2 + 17*384) = 5,328,000 + emb 41,088 + head 41,088 + ln_f 768 = 5,410,944 (vocab 107); slopes buffer is not a parameter; CPU check of sum(p.numel() for p in model.parameters()) = 5,410,944
arch.n_layers_detail: 6 logical applications, 3 unique PeriLN blocks (A-B-C-A-B-C), same as 125-fable at width 384
arch.checkpoint_reconstruction: ALiBiGPT(vocab, 6, 384, 8) from this pretrain.py, then blocks = ModuleList(unique * 2) of 3 PeriLNBlock(384, 8) with the same object aliases before load_state_dict (state_dict repeats the shared blocks under blocks.0/3, 1/4, 2/5 keys)
arch.kv_cache: 6 caches, one per logical application (sample.generate builds one per model.blocks entry), each (B, 8, max, 48); caches[0] also holds key positions for the ALiBi bias as in 115-fable; CPU check: cached vs full forward max abs diff ~1e-6

optimizer.name: split-QKV Muon (RMS-matched shape scale, relative to D=384) with Polar Express orthogonalization on the 3 unique blocks' 12 matrices and head.weight; AdamW on embeddings, biases and LayerNorm params (unchanged from 129-claude)
optimizer.schedule: cosine over wall-clock with floor 0.3 (unchanged from 129-claude): after 200 warmup steps lr = 1e-3*(0.3 + 0.35*(1+cos(pi*frac)))

data.augmentation: random ref shift (lean_seq names n1.. share one start offset per row)

config.init: fork default (normal 0.02, zero biases) then orthogonal_(gain=0.02*sqrt(max(shape))) on the 3 unique blocks' matrices; emb/head normal 0.02
